q: A system call is used to:
options: Switch the CPU from user mode to kernel mode to request a service from the OS
Call a function defined in your own C file
Permanently stay in kernel mode for speed
explain: System call user mode se kernel mode mein trap ke through jaata hai taaki OS se koi service (file, process) maang sake.

q: Which kernel type keeps most services like drivers and file system inside the kernel for speed?
explain: Monolithic kernel (jaise Linux) mein zyada services kernel ke andar hoti hain, isliye fast par ek bug poore kernel ko gira sakta hai.

q: The mode bit value for kernel mode and user mode respectively is usually:
explain: Convention: 0 = kernel mode (full power), 1 = user mode (limited power).

options: Multitasking needs multiple CPUs, multiprocessing uses one CPU
Multitasking is fast switching on one CPU, multiprocessing truly runs on multiple CPUs
They mean exactly the same thing
explain: Multitasking ek CPU par time-slice switching hai; multiprocessing mein sach mein kai CPU/cores saath chalte hain.

q: During booting, which process is started first by the kernel as PID 1?
explain: Kernel sab initialise karke pehla user process init/systemd (PID 1) start karta hai, jisse baaki processes bante hain.
